# Overview

Four pages of the Viewer show tables and plots stored in the `.crb` file. Each
page appears in the sidebar only when the loaded data set contains its content.

| Page | Shows | Filled by |
|---|---|---|
| Most expressed genes | the 100 genes with the largest share of all transcripts in each group | `getMostExpressedGenes()`; the `convert*()` functions add them on their own |
| Marker genes | genes that distinguish a group from the other groups | `getMarkerGenes()`, or your own table |
| Enriched pathways | pathway and gene set enrichment results per group | `getEnrichedPathways()`, `performGeneSetEnrichmentAnalysis()`, or your own table |
| Extra material | any other tables, and plots made with ggplot2 | your own tables and plots |

`exportFromSeurat()` computes none of these tables itself: it writes what the
Seurat object carries. Without them, the first three pages stay hidden.

# In the Viewer

On **Marker genes**, **Most expressed genes** and **Enriched pathways**, choose
the grouping variable, and for marker genes and pathways the method. When the
first column of a table is that grouping variable, **Filter results for
subgroup** shows one group at a time; switch on **Show results for all
subgroups (no pre-filtering)** to see the whole table. For data sets made with
a `convert*()` function, **Most expressed genes** can also show the mean
expression per group.

The tables can be searched and sorted, and **Download** saves them as CSV or
Excel files. Where they appear, **Automatically format numbers** and
**Highlight values with colours** change only how the values are shown.

On **Extra material**, choose between tables and plots, then the item. Plots
are converted to interactive plotly graphics. If the conversion misses
something, such as a legend, switch off **Make plot interactive** to see the
ggplot2 plot as it was made.

# Compute the tables

For a Seurat object, the CerebroNexus functions store their results in the
object's `@misc` slot, where `exportFromSeurat()` picks them up. This example
uses `pbmc_small`, which ships with Seurat:

```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(CerebroNexus)

data("pbmc_small")
seurat <- UpdateSeuratObject(pbmc_small)
seurat$seurat_clusters <- seurat$RNA_snn_res.1

seurat <- getMostExpressedGenes(
  seurat,
  assay = "RNA",
  groups = c("seurat_clusters", "groups")
)
seurat <- getMarkerGenes(
  seurat,
  assay = "RNA",
  organism = "hg",
  groups = c("seurat_clusters", "groups"),
  name = "cerebro_seurat",
  only_pos = TRUE
)
```

For enriched pathways, run `getEnrichedPathways()` on the marker genes (it
queries the Enrichr web service) or `performGeneSetEnrichmentAnalysis()` with
your own gene sets; see
[Introduction to the CerebroNexus workflow (Seurat)](cerebronexus_workflow_seurat.html).

`convertSeuratToCerebro()`, `convertSCEToCerebro()` and `convertH5adToCerebro()`
add the most expressed genes and the mean expression per group on their own
(`add_most_expressed_genes = TRUE`). They can read a marker gene table from a
file (`marker_file`), and `convertH5adToCerebro()` takes the marker genes that
scanpy ranked; see
[Show your Seurat, scanpy and SingleCellExperiment analysis with CerebroNexus](import_your_analysis.html).

# Add your own tables and plots

## In a Seurat object

Put your results in `@misc` before the export. Marker genes and enriched
pathways are lists of methods, each a list of tables named by grouping
variable. Extra material holds `tables` (data frames) and `plots` (ggplot2
objects):

```{r}
my_markers <- data.frame(
  seurat_clusters = c("0", "1"),
  gene = c("CD3E", "MS4A1"),
  score = c(2.1, 1.7)
)
seurat@misc$marker_genes$my_method <- list(seurat_clusters = my_markers)

my_pathways <- data.frame(
  seurat_clusters = "0",
  term = "T cell activation",
  p_value = 0.001
)
seurat@misc$enriched_pathways$my_enrichment <- list(
  seurat_clusters = my_pathways
)

seurat@misc$extra_material <- list(
  tables = list(
    cell_counts = as.data.frame(table(cluster = seurat$seurat_clusters))
  ),
  plots = list(
    dot_plot = DotPlot(
      seurat,
      features = c("CD3E", "MS4A1", "LYZ"),
      group.by = "seurat_clusters"
    )
  )
)

exportFromSeurat(
  seurat,
  assay = "RNA",
  slot = "data",
  file = "pbmc_tables.crb",
  experiment_name = "pbmc",
  organism = "hg",
  groups = c("seurat_clusters", "groups"),
  nUMI = "nCount_RNA",
  nGene = "nFeature_RNA"
)
```

A marker gene table may have any name and any columns. An enriched pathways
table is kept only when its name is one of the exported `groups`. Name the
first column after the grouping variable, as above, so that the Viewer can
filter the table by group.

## In an existing `.crb` file

Data sets from scanpy or SingleCellExperiment have no `@misc` slot. Add tables
and plots to the `.crb` file instead, with the methods of the Cerebro object:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

crb <- readCerebro("pbmc_tables.crb")
cells <- crb$getMetaData()

crb$addExtraTable(
  "cells_per_cluster",
  as.data.frame(table(cluster = cells$seurat_clusters))
)
crb$addExtraPlot(
  "cells_per_cluster",
  ggplot(cells, aes(seurat_clusters)) + geom_bar()
)
saveCerebro(crb, "pbmc_tables.crb")
```

`addMarkerGenes()`, `addEnrichedPathways()` and `addMostExpressedGenes()` add
the other tables; see `?Cerebro`.

## For one generated app only

`createShinyApp(extra_tables = ...)` adds CSV, TSV or Excel files to the Extra
material page of a generated app without changing the `.crb` file; see
[External Extra material tables](create_a_self_contained_shiny_app.html#external-extra-material-tables).

# Open the result

```{r}
launchCerebro(crb_file_to_load = "pbmc_tables.crb")
```
